fun_facts: DeSean Bishop’s hometown is Knoxville, Tennessee.
He starred at Karns High School in Knoxville—close to the University of Tennessee.
Against Georgia Tech in 2026, he rushed for 147 yards and two touchdowns.
In 2026, he became just the second player in Tennessee history to post 1,000-yard rushing seasons back to back; the first was Johnnie Jones in 1983–84.
Over two seasons, 947 of his 1,531 rushing yards came after contact, and he forced 47 missed tackles.

basis.reasoning: The recruiting profile identifies Knoxville as Bishop’s hometown. ESPN’s 2026 player feature says he starred at Karns High School in Knoxville. ESPN’s Georgia Tech recap reports 147 rushing yards and two touchdowns. The 2026 player feature also gives his two-season yards-after-contact and forced-missed-tackle totals.

excerpts:
If they hope to salvage their season, the Aggies will have to find a way to slow down running back [DeSean Bishop](http://www.espn.com/college-football/player/_/id/4921108/desean-bishop) .

He had 109 yards rushing with two scores on Saturday to eclipse 1,000 yards for a second straight season, making him just the second player in school history with consecutive 1,000-yard seasons and the first since Johnnie Jones (1983-84).

Bishop ranks second in the SEC and 10th in the nation by averaging 118.4 yards a game and his 13 rushing scores are also second-most in the league and rank seventh nationally.
